plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single labeled diagram of an upward-opening parabola drawn on a Cartesian coordinate plane, with thin black arrowed axes crossing near the lower left of the curve and marked x at the right and y at the top. The parabola is a heavy dark blue curve whose two branches end in arrowheads pointing up and outward. Its lowest point is a filled dark blue dot above the horizontal x-axis, connected by a short leader line to the label Vertex at the left. A dashed orange vertical line rises through that dot and carries the orange label Axis of symmetry at the upper right. Directly above the vertex on that same vertical line sits a small teal dot labeled Focus in teal. A short dashed blue horizontal segment runs through the teal dot from one branch of the curve to the other and is tagged Latus rectum by a curved arrow from the upper left. Below the vertex, a dashed red horizontal line spanning the width of the frame is labeled Directrix in red, and the x-axis lies lower in the frame. Color-coding the four named features separately lets the reader see that the axis of symmetry meets the directrix at a right angle and that the vertex lies midway between focus and directrix. The drawing establishes the vocabulary used to define a parabola as the set of points equally distant from the focus and the directrix.

interactionPlan.concept: A parabola is the set of points equally distant from a fixed focus and a fixed directrix, and the focus-to-directrix distance p alone determines how wide the curve opens.
elements: x-axis with arrowhead, labeled x
y-axis with arrowhead, labeled y
heavy dark blue upward-opening parabola with arrowheads on both branches
vertex: filled dark blue dot at the curve's lowest point, labeled 'Vertex' with leader line
axis of symmetry: dashed orange vertical line through the vertex, labeled 'Axis of symmetry'
focus: small teal dot above the vertex on the axis of symmetry, labeled 'Focus'
latus rectum: short dashed blue horizontal segment through the focus spanning branch to branch, labeled 'Latus rectum' with curved arrow
directrix: dashed red horizontal line below the vertex, labeled 'Directrix'
distance-construction view: movable sample point on the curve with perpendicular segment to focus and perpendicular segment to directrix, shown equal in length
p-distance bracket between focus and directrix in the construction view

interactions.label: Focus–directrix distance p
interactions.teaches: The focus and directrix stay symmetric about the vertex, and increasing p widens the parabola while decreasing p narrows it — the equal-distance definition alone fixes the curve's shape.

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: Every point on the parabola is equidistant from the focus and the directrix, which is why the vertex — the closest point — must sit exactly midway between them.
Each vocabulary term (vertex, focus, directrix, axis of symmetry, latus rectum) is highlighted with its label on demand, keeping the diagram uncluttered while clarifying what each feature is.

demo_steps.title: Meet the features
demo_steps.narration: An upward-opening parabola with its named parts color-coded: vertex at the bottom, focus above it, directrix below, and the axis of symmetry running vertically through all of them. Hover each feature to identify it.

demo_steps.title: Stretch with p
demo_steps.narration: Drag p larger and smaller: the focus rises as the directrix mirrors below, and the blue curve widens or narrows — the single distance p controls the entire shape.

demo_steps.title: Why the vertex is the midpoint
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the construction view: from a sample point on the curve, the segment to the focus and the perpendicular segment to the directrix are equal in length. At the vertex both segments collapse to the same vertical line, so it must lie exactly halfway between focus and directrix.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Every point on a parabola is equally far from the focus and the directrix — so the vertex sits at their midpoint and the distance p between them alone determines the curve's width.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Upward-opening dark blue parabola centered on a dashed orange vertical axis of symmetry, drawn over black arrowed x and y axes with the origin below and left of the curve. Vertex is a filled dark blue dot slightly above the x-axis; focus a teal dot directly above it on the axis; directrix a dashed red horizontal line below the vertex, mirroring the focus distance. Latus rectum is a dashed blue chord through the focus. Labels color-matched to their features: 'Axis of symmetry' orange, 'Focus' teal, 'Directrix' red, 'Latus rectum' blue, 'Vertex' dark blue. In construction view, fade the labels and show a highlighted sample point on one branch with a segment to the focus and a perpendicular drop to the directrix, both drawn in matching color with equal-length tick marks; also show a small p bracket spanning focus to directrix. The parabola must be recomputed from the definition (equal distance) as p changes, so widening/narrowing is geometrically faithful, with the vertex fixed on screen and focus/directrix moving symmetrically.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for changing the focus-directrix distance p: the learner drags p, the focus rises or falls with the directrix mirroring below the vertex and the blue parabola widens or narrows, making the equal-distance definition control the curve's shape.
- Toggle between labeled features and distance construction: the learner switches views, labels fade into perpendicular distance segments from a sample point to the focus and directrix, making clear why the vertex sits midway between them.
- Hover for individual parabola features: the learner hovers the vertex, focus, directrix, axis, or latus rectum, the selected feature brightens with its label and related construction lines, clarifying each vocabulary term without crowding the diagram.

authoredContext:
In Quadratic Functions, we learned about a parabola’s vertex and axis of symmetry. Now we extend the discussion to include other key features of the parabola. See the figure. Notice that the axis of symmetry passes through the focus and vertex and is perpendicular to the directrix. The vertex is the midpoint between the directrix and the focus.

The line segment that passes through the focus and is parallel to the directrix is called the latus rectum. The endpoints of the latus rectum lie on the curve. By definition, the distance d from the focus to any point P on the parabola is equal to the distance from P to the directrix.

Key features of the parabola

This image displays a parabola on a Cartesian coordinate plane, clearly labeling its fundamental geometric elements. The blue curve represents the parabola itself. The "Vertex" is indicated as the turning point of the parabola. Inside the curve, the "Focus" is marked, a critical point for defining the parabola. A dashed orange line, labeled "Axis of symmetry", passes vertically through both the vertex and the focus. Below the vertex, a horizontal dashed red line shows the "Directrix". Finally, a horizontal dashed blue line segment passing through the focus and extending to the parabola is identified as the "Latus rectum".

To work with parabolas in the coordinate plane, we consider two cases: those with a vertex at the origin and those with a vertex at a point other than the origin. We begin with the former.

discrepancies: the 'Directrix' label sits directly on the x-axis line at the right edge, colliding with the axis and its arrowhead, whereas the source places it clearly above the dashed directrix line
the 'Axis of symmetry' label is pushed to the top-right of the axis line and risks clipping, rather than being placed mid-height beside the dashed line as in the source

the source shows the focus dot sitting just above the vertex with the x-axis passing below the directrix region; in the generated figure the directrix nearly coincides with the x-axis, compressing the vertex–focus–directrix spacing at default p
evaluation.notes: A faithful parabola-features figure with correct color coding, dashed axis/directrix, arrow-tipped curve, and strong pedagogy via the p slider, construction toggle, and demo steps; main flaws are label collisions with the x-axis and cramped focus–directrix spacing at default p.
action_items: Move the 'Directrix' label off the x-axis (e.g. just above or below the dashed red line, left of the axis arrowhead) so it no longer overlaps the axis artwork.
Reposition the 'Axis of symmetry' label beside the dashed orange line at mid-height and inside the plot bounds, matching the source placement.
Increase the default vertical separation between vertex, focus, and directrix (or shift the origin) so the directrix does not nearly coincide with the x-axis at p=1.5.

feedback.rationale: Scores are consistently high (4-5, average 4.4) with correct concept and interactivity; the remaining issues are minor label-placement polish that do not justify another iteration.
